subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3 Consolidation: Grammar file and Practice Guide
outcomes: Correct mistakes with future forms (will, going to, present continuous).
Tell the difference between advice and suggestions.
Use exam strategies for gapped texts, picture listening and speaking.

tf.s: We use 'I'll' for an offer, like 'I'll go to the shop. Do you need anything?'
tf.why: Yes, will is great for offers.

tf.s: 'The train leaves at 6.30 tomorrow' uses the present simple for a timetable.
tf.why: Timetables use the present simple, even for the future.

tf.s: 'How about to have some sandwiches?' is correct.
tf.why: After 'How about' we use -ing: 'How about having some sandwiches?'

tf.s: 'You should see a doctor' is a suggestion.
When we can see something is about to happen, we use 'going to'.
tf.why: Like 'Look out! That cat's going to jump!'

tf.s: We use 'Shall I…?' to make an offer.
In a gapped-text task, you should read only the sentence before the gap.
tf.why: Read the sentences before AND after the gap.

tf.s: In picture listening, you often hear about all three pictures, but only one answers the question.
tf.why: So listen carefully to the whole recording.

tf.s: In the Unit 3 gapped-text tasks, there are no extra sentences.
tf.why: There are three extra sentences you don't need.

tf.s: 'What do you think?' is a phrase to ask your partner's opinion.
tf.why: Asking your partner keeps the discussion going.

boxes.q: Bader and I arranged it. Complete: Bader and I ___ to the cinema tonight.
boxes.why: We use the present continuous for arrangements.

boxes.q: Complete the suggestion: Why ___ we go to the park?
Complete the offer: ___ I help you?
The sky is clear. Complete: I don't think it ___ rain tomorrow.
boxes.why: 'I don't think it will…' is the correct prediction.

boxes.q: What should you look for around a gap?

o: name each picture and predict words

boxes.q: Complete the suggestion: You ___ try this new app – it's great!
In the collaborative speaking task, you try to…
boxes.why: Talk with your partner and agree together.

boxes.q: Complete the arrangement: I ___ meeting my friends at four.

hunt.q: Look out! The cat's going to ___!
Read the sentences before and ___ the gap.
Ask an opinion: What do you ___?
Plan: I'm going to ___ a book tonight.

mcq.q: Which form do we often use for a fixed arrangement with a time?
Which strategy helps with a gapped text?
o: Read the sentences before and after the gap
Leave all the hard gaps empty
mcq.why: The text around the gap gives you clues.

mcq.q: Which phrase asks for your partner's view?
mcq.why: This phrase invites your partner to give an opinion.

mcq.q: Correct the offer: 'I go to the shop. Do you need anything?'
mcq.why: We use will for offers made now.

mcq.q: Your friend has a headache. Give advice.
Complete: I'm sure our team ___ win. They're the best!
mcq.why: We use will for a prediction we feel sure about.

mcq.q: Why is 'leaves' correct in 'The train leaves at 6.30 tomorrow'?
o: It is a timetable, so we use the present simple.

mcq.q: In picture listening, why must you listen carefully until the end?
o: All three things may be mentioned, but only one is the answer.
You hear nothing about the pictures.
The answer is always the first picture.

mcq.q: Why do we use 'going to' in 'Look out! That cat's going to jump!'?
o: We can see it is about to happen.
mcq.why: We use going to when we can see the evidence now.
